candidates.comment: Thanks for the report. This was fixed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/43c3a69a40c390e34b724f779feffde8796f969d: adding or removing workspace folders no longer replaces or deletes an active session through provisional-session cleanup. Closing as completed; this prevents further destruction but does not restore previously deleted conversations. The fix shipped in 1.144.0.

Thanks for the report. The brighter legacy tab backgrounds were fixed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/ab8f31f0c0b1a4dd86d8dbee1248542f5806574d: Dark Modern's `editorGroupHeader.tabsBackground` and `tab.inactiveBackground` are restored to `#181818`, while connected tabs retain their separate palette. This resolves the original color regression; the later concern about separation between inactive tabs is distinct from that color restoration. The fix shipped in 1.140.0.

Thanks for the report and the workaround details. The SDK download deadlock was fixed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/e3c3c4524e85a24bbe0066cee5cfe3c6c0ec8532: a missing SDK now has a reachable Download action regardless of GitHub sign-in, and installation refreshes Claude models and session discovery. The confirmation above that automatic SDK upgrades work on 1.140.0-insider supports closing this report as resolved; the two earlier Claude issues remain separate. The fix shipped in 1.138.0.

Thanks for the detailed report. Historical reasoning replay was added in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/c1ce6113b81a6e2359e10e4ad0fc81d3298e8deb, and ID-less reasoning preservation was fixed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/525e4082a6b54d5e56c04b7a9c9b00125ec10686. Kimi K3 enables historical replay automatically. For other models that require preserved thinking, set `"github.copilot.chat.modelCapabilityOverrides": { "<model-id>": { "thinkingInHistory": true } }` in settings, retaining `"thinking": true` in the model configuration. Extension-contributed providers must also declare the Chat Completions API through their model capabilities. These changes address the two loss mechanisms described here; replay remains restricted to the same model. The fix shipped in 1.141.0.

Thanks for the detailed report. This is addressed by https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/0b49fec181fe9415a9aa5b0315c32863b84a83d3: disconnecting a web tunnel now keeps the host available while pausing automatic reconnection, including after reload. Open Connection Information beside the host picker and use Connect to reconnect without editing browser storage. The fix shipped in 1.139.0.

Thanks for the accessibility feedback. https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/301c31b679b3313439f01cdf9cd1d6c63d70d34b introduced Connected tabs: the active tab shares the editor background and joins the document, while inactive tabs use the tab-strip background. This is now the Modern UI default, available explicitly through `"workbench.experimental.modernUIEditorTabStyle": "connected"`, so the central concern reported here has been addressed. The fix shipped in 1.139.0.

Thanks for the detailed investigation and corrections. The session-list summary was changed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/6fd2d2e178f1d98c534809cf63236f7d8f040412: folder sessions now derive their counts from Session Changes, including multi-folder aggregation, rather than the branch's divergence. Worktree sessions intentionally retain Branch Changes. Previously cached counts for unopened sessions can remain until the session is opened and its summary recomputed. This addresses the session-list behavior reported here. The fix shipped in 1.138.0.

Thanks for the report, including the detail about accidental tab closures. This was addressed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/851a360639cd70543a2ef6e19b921ac1d226118d: Modern UI tabs reserve a separate column for the close control instead of placing it over the filename. Current VS Code also provides `"workbench.editor.tabActionReserveSpace": true` (the default) to retain that separation. The fix shipped in 1.134.0.

Thanks for the report and the additional endpoint-grouping context. https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/d0d9e149c575c69f840768674a0a10cb97ff1030 preserves the configured endpoint in Agent Host model identities and routes each selection to its exact endpoint, so models sharing an ID remain separately selectable. https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/d4e3d3ed14b25746a3502b3f409119bc4ebbd254 also resolves configured endpoint names for picker grouping. These changes cover the reported behavior; please let us know if either symptom persists on the latest build. The fix shipped in 1.133.0.

Thanks for the request. Claude conversation-content export is wired into Agent Host in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/9bf25de7927cadb3f4f2ce7ee93de18aee64c4da, and Claude session-title spans were added in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/40b268f373d01d3bc708301c6f4ab20e8a02848a. Enable `chat.agentHost.otel.enabled` and `chat.agentHost.otel.captureContent` with your OTel destination to capture user prompts, assistant responses, and title changes. For external title export, use OTLP/HTTP JSON; titles are also available locally in DB mode. Content capture remains off by default. The fix shipped in 1.133.0.

Thanks for the report. The modal-creation race was fixed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/b8d3a33d7387e4e8fb371c3f55c2462287799d03: opening multiple recommended extensions concurrently now reuses one modal editor instead of creating overlapping overlays. This can be closed as completed. The fix shipped in 1.131.0.

Thanks for the report. The requested revert landed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/77f8b67c2c1eced2ae12e3e0a1dbbca311abafa0 and shipped in 1.126.0, restoring the previous neutral colors for ordinary variables and the broad token scopes affected by the change. Closing this as completed; the later feedback about variables needing more differentiation is tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/331473.

Thanks for the request. Visual Studio 2026 detection was added in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/35c48f9946eecf40beed751940607f184a03b6de: the preinstall check now recognizes its `Microsoft Visual Studio\18` installation directory and supports `vs2026_install` for custom locations. This addresses the reported preinstall restriction. The fix shipped in 1.142.0.

Thanks for the report. The “Response too long” failure in the Copilot model wrapper was fixed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/f85c5317641ec85d817ce1d03551c66bd4782ecc: Ollama/BYOK responses ending with a length finish reason now retain their streamed output instead of failing the request. This resolves the reported exception; it does not establish why the separate curl request returned a different finish reason. The fix shipped in 1.128.0.

Thanks for the report. This was fixed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/6a932e0f957fb194b0ffa81b8bb51080aa274147: completed Mermaid diagrams now remain mounted while subsequent response text streams, preventing the repeated iframe reloads and diagram flicker. The fix shipped in 1.139.0.

Thanks for the detailed report. This chat-path issue was addressed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/0d4262ebcd31fd1f7e508469712999bda39f31fe: custom endpoints now forward adaptive-thinking configuration and preserve request-level thinking enablement, so your Messages configuration can send `thinking: {"type":"adaptive","display":"summarized"}`. Closing as completed. The fix shipped in 1.134.0.

Thanks for the report and the crash diagnostics. This startup crash matches the screen-source warm-up regression fixed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/66b0ebffcac05bf48961964735e3be4c3c963ec4 and shipped in 1.122.1: VS Code no longer enumerates screen-capture sources during startup. The same crash was confirmed resolved in later Insiders builds at https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/318063#issuecomment-4611524055, so this can be closed as completed.

Thanks for the report. This was fixed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/199bf7e55222baca85bc6f56d0bba8320b247841, after the May 5 build you reported: “Enable AI Features (Workspace)” now saves an explicit workspace override for `chat.disableAIFeatures`, so reopening that workspace keeps AI enabled while other workspaces remain disabled. The fix shipped in 1.120.0.

Thanks for the request. File references using @ are now implemented for new and existing Agents Window sessions in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/5788cd3ebf8b075618ac923bb109df5ab761246b. Typing @ followed by a workspace filename offers matching files, and selecting one attaches its reference to the conversation. The fix shipped in 1.120.0.

Thanks for the detailed report. The startup update-client code that launched this command was removed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/4ab3c68fb34db270e470ebdfd07b9086e8b0851c, merged through https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/316264. Routine startup cleanup no longer launches that PowerShell command, so this can be closed as fixed. Installer-time context-menu cleanup is separate and still uses PowerShell. The fix shipped in 1.121.0.

Thanks for the report. This was fixed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/7969885bfc67fe72418d87ecf3c4e0092b83bf54: the notification now counts only recommendations that resolve to marketplace plugins, fetching the marketplace first when the cache is empty. When no matching plugins are available, the notification is suppressed. The fix shipped in 1.121.0.

Thanks for the context. External Copilot CLI session discovery was implemented in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/6f96a7816c2a7b68d26b65a353c411912fee7b30: the Agent Host distinguishes discovered external sessions from VS Code-owned sessions. The shared `chat.agentSessions.showExternal` setting now controls which external sessions appear; set it to `none` to hide them. This covers the discovery and filtering requested here. The fix shipped in 1.134.0.

Thanks for the report. This packaging omission was fixed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/baedb11a87e9c4cf334a3114eb4b3d7d53e67fe0: the extension package now includes sdk/definitions/sidekick/*.yaml, including github-context.yaml, addressing the missing-file error when opening a Copilot CLI session. The fix shipped in 1.120.0.

Thanks for the report and contribution. Your fix landed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/318148 as https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/93c53e6fc5c0da18cfd254ff7a35a14b2ffae6f6: reading existing notebook cell outputs now uses the real token budget and the corrected size threshold, so small outputs are no longer rejected as too large. This can be closed as completed. The fix shipped in 1.123.0.

Thanks for the report. Harness selection persistence was implemented in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/154bcccdf299a90df2c3ef3d629a25439cdbc926. The new-session flow now remembers an explicit Claude selection and reuses it when Claude is available for the selected folder, so this can be closed as completed. The fix shipped in 1.120.0.

Thanks for the report. This was fixed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/dbadc07b699a363fb4dcd45271a44da986bd691d: Install Plugin from Source now resolves the Extensions service before the asynchronous install handler, so revealing a successfully installed plugin no longer accesses an expired service accessor. The fix shipped in 1.118.0.

Thanks for the report. The code-review version calculation responsible for this exception, including its session-opening autorun, was removed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/57dd1589153beba6f43041da8e5f430f9da3d2f4. The build cited in the July recurrence predates that change, and the failing path is no longer present on current main, so this can be closed as completed. The fix shipped in 1.125.0.

Thanks for the request. Tool inspection and configuration were added in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/63ba2ff5250c9bff0324fd49845eedec375a0361. In the Agents window, open Chat Customizations > Tools to inspect tool descriptions and enable or disable individual configurable tools or whole groups; Copilot's built-in tools are listed as Always Available. This covers the requested UI, so this can be closed as completed. The fix shipped in 1.127.0.

Thanks for the report. This was fixed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/b713893016bbc5e28e37369e37852ec1f4a522ae by applying the terminal background to the full editor wrapper as well as the inner code block, removing the uncovered strip on the right. The fix shipped in 1.116.0.

Thanks for the report. This is covered by https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/93c53e6fc5c0da18cfd254ff7a35a14b2ffae6f6, which corrects the notebook-output size checks and gives output-reading calls the actual prompt budget instead of a one-token placeholder. Small text outputs can now be passed to Copilot for explanation, so this can be closed as fixed. The fix shipped in 1.123.0.

Thanks for the report and design discussion. This was addressed by https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/0dcf0529d4662e50084195cd356da6c508c5e234: model-picker rows can now render their hover content together with configuration submenu actions, so a reasoning-effort menu no longer hides the degraded-model message. Current main also carries the CAPI degradation reason through to the model warning banner and selected-model status hover. The fix shipped in 1.117.0.

Thanks for the report. This was fixed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/837b3f6f130d8ff97e6de24b645ee4a51af6a03e: error confirmations now treat the preceding response as actionable even when queued or steering messages appear below it, so the Try Again button remains visible. The follow-up https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/debbc28b7d59c0317a3ac61cbbc018fa7c3431d8 retained that behavior while correcting the queued-row layout. The fix shipped in 1.128.0.

Thanks for the report. This `RangeError: Invalid string length` path was addressed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/eb308be4f9d2ce27a4117d84b7a789d90dd6cd62: chat-session persistence now retries with bounded truncation rather than losing the entire session when serialized content exceeds V8's string limit. The matching report at https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/308843 was closed by https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/319183, so this can be closed as completed. The fix shipped in 1.123.0.

Thanks for the report. The missing native-module path was fixed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/17c5c32122f71707abd6ea0f8f3265fd5f161680: Copilot CLI now copies VS Code's platform-native node-pty files into the SDK's expected `prebuilds/<platform>-<arch>` directory before importing the SDK. Please open a new issue with current-version logs if this still occurs. The fix shipped in 1.119.0.

Thanks for the report. The missing native `pty.node` path for separately installed Copilot Chat extensions was fixed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/17c5c32122f71707abd6ea0f8f3265fd5f161680; current VS Code copies the matching node-pty binary into the Copilot SDK layout before loading it. The fix shipped in 1.119.0.

Thanks for the report and the revert. https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/0592154b3ecc1d1d43367c85751a7b9bda88d470 restored string option IDs for the Copilot CLI provider, addressing the worktree-creation regression identified here. That conversion remains in the current code, so this can be closed as completed. The fix shipped in 1.113.0.

Thanks for the report. This was addressed by https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/8d96288bfc5fd31d3895ae509435b0071f1082b1: `chat.plugins.marketplaces` now defaults to `github/awesome-copilot#marketplace`, and discovery honors that branch. Its `.github/plugin/marketplace.json` is available and contains the plugin catalog, so discovery no longer relies on the missing `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` URL. The fix shipped in 1.123.0.

Thanks for the report and investigation. https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/7b17c65f78d7c39e4e06fb924a2002949b9861c4 changed terminal handling so resolved Cmd shortcuts are intercepted before Kitty keyboard reporting can send them to the application, covering the Cmd+C input-leak path described here. The separate problem where pressing a modifier clears the selection before copying remains tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/336506. The fix shipped in 1.113.0.

Thanks for the report. https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/7867731f8eacdca0f1992b07de9e7c318ecac9e6 restores frosted backgrounds for the Command Palette and Quick Open through the shared Modern UI overlay styling. The effect uses `workbench.experimental.modernUI` and `workbench.modernUIFrostedGlass`; `workbench.modernUIFrostedGlassOpacity` controls transparency, while reduced-transparency preferences, high-contrast themes, and unsupported graphics intentionally keep solid backgrounds. The fix shipped in 1.141.0.

Thanks for the report. This was fixed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/0db3a09a29630bed7069576e5ad00cb97536b36d: Backspace now removes a single character when correcting a manually typed slash command. Immediately backspacing a command inserted through autocomplete still removes the inserted token. The fix shipped in 1.115.0.

Thanks for the request. The interactive session visualization was added in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/c4c215b11f52dc2c45bb1aa54ba430215ed8e4e0. Run **Open Agent Debug Logs** (`workbench.action.chat.openAgentDebugPanel`), select a session, and choose **Agent Flow Chart** to explore context-discovery events, tool calls, and nested subagent activity, with collapsible sections and selectable event details. This covers the requested visualization. The fix shipped in 1.110.1.

Thanks for the detailed report. This flow was fixed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/e2db4495b34a5bd799b29824fc8d12eb5082545f: custom prompt submissions now retain the original `/foo` invocation instead of rewriting it to a raw `vscode-userdata` Markdown link, so editing and resubmitting resolves and attaches the prompt file again. The fix shipped in 1.112.0.

Thanks for the context. The requested BYOK stream extension was implemented in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/2e3f347c80edcd93738b39071ef9fa93394c7656: providers emit token usage as a `LanguageModelDataPart` with MIME type `usage`, and the consuming endpoint decodes those counts into the chat response. This covers the stream-extension request, so this can be closed as completed. The fix shipped in 1.120.0.

Thanks for the request. This was implemented in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/04b756ba9f07d7232d9199c5d78f74a7e7eb164a: Auto now shows a routing status in the chat and names the selected model as soon as routing resolves, before the response completes. The fix shipped in 1.128.0.

Thanks for the context. The Cloud Agent Tasks API is implemented, and https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/cd5814553ec9b1e40fae681e1163199a23b16480 completed the switch away from the legacy backend. Cloud sessions now use task identities and can run without a pull request, with PR creation available separately, so this implementation request can be closed as completed. The fix shipped in 1.134.0.

Thanks for the report. This was addressed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/0f16e7f7830f658ab3f529ad0a6a41bfb7917da5: the sessions pane's New Session button now targets its own chat pane instead of the last-focused widget, so it no longer sends focus back to the welcome input. The fix shipped in 1.126.0.

Thanks for the report. This was fixed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/6a12c4553b4fa16d6ff344682b3bdca0ce0fcbf2: the Agent Sessions Welcome product-name heading now has an explicit line-height so its lines no longer overlap when resizing makes it wrap. The fix shipped in 1.114.0.

Thanks for the context. This was addressed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/5b46a7924f8fcd97253154f602223e71f7dd3aa5: sendChatRequest now accepts undefined for the extension identifier, and the internal callers listed here no longer construct ExtensionIdentifier('core'). The fix shipped in 1.111.0.

Thanks for the context. This prompt change is implemented in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/a3ebc7b2f2d725e088c24bee7ca974a8071964f7: `run_in_terminal` now strongly prefers `mode='sync'` for one-shot commands and reserves `mode='async'` for indefinitely running servers, watchers, and daemons. The legacy `isBackground` flag is deprecated in favor of `mode`, so this prompt-tweaking request can be closed as completed; agent-controlled background conversion remains tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/288566. The fix shipped in 1.125.0.

Thanks for the report. The repeated warnings were fixed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/b824fac5492ab42158b5ca4e81870e0205e53473 via https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/287546: model duplication is now checked only after clearing and rebuilding that vendor's cache, rather than during each resolution pass. This should no longer flood the log while scrolling through chat. The fix shipped in 1.109.0.

Thanks for the report. This was addressed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/8d8f1028df37be745a244f27fb300ed12272fa57: the recording icon and pulse now use `editorInfo.foreground`, which has blue defaults in light and dark themes, instead of the activity-bar foreground. High-contrast themes retain their contrast-specific color. The fix shipped in 1.126.0.

Thanks for the report. This was fixed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/60869c766646abcd55bc396882a98f67aea15fc5 via https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/285112: choosing Copy All from an AI search result now copies the AI search results rather than the ordinary search results. This can be closed as completed. The fix shipped in 1.109.0.

Thanks for the report. https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/8e70e1e590fd93ed39877a769bf976e8fef67233 changes saved session status so an interrupted tool confirmation is recorded as cancelled, rather than continuing to show that input is needed after restart. This addresses the stale indicator; continuing the confirmation itself across a reload remains a separate capability. The fix shipped in 1.109.0.

Thanks for the report. This was fixed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/d529467855d6a6ae194471f1a2817f0d731feced: the URL approval picker now lists each shared pattern once when fetching multiple URLs from the same domain. The fix shipped in 1.108.0.

Thanks for the cleanup request. The local session controller now observes chat models directly, and the remaining `registerChatModelChangeListeners` helper was removed from the service interface and implementation in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/dd1cba93568028144d73f56f24fe0705bda19014. This completes the remaining cleanup identified in the January discussion. The fix shipped in 1.114.0.

Thanks for the detailed logs. The failing `Readable.fromWeb(resp.body)` bridge was removed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/a2a163471d5bc3adf346564f4f99fe6fce48db65, and the replacement stream handling shipped in 1.116.0, so this should be resolved on current versions.

Thanks for the report. This was fixed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/69e459e483605a9b93acdb08a90d5a0798a09eef: signature help now follows TypeScript's updated overload recommendation as you type, rather than retaining the initially displayed overload. For your example, typing func("three", should select signature 3/4 without dismissing and reopening the tooltip. The fix shipped in 1.132.0.

Thanks for the request. Manage Models now includes an **Install Model Providers** button that opens the Extensions Marketplace with `tag:"language-models"`, providing the discovery entry point discussed here. This was implemented in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/9c64fc03ba3679db7dbb0b7812fa3d75d9dab42b, so this can be closed as completed. The fix shipped in 1.125.0.

Thanks for the report. This was addressed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/9dadd5ad1defcc3140bcdff44517284aeaf5bb91 by removing the Snap launcher's `XDG_DATA_HOME` override, so new Explorer deletions are no longer redirected to the Snap-specific trash directory. The fix does not automatically clear files already accumulated in that directory; closing this as completed for the incorrect trash routing. The fix shipped in 1.139.0.

Thanks for the request. This is now available as **Chat: Manage Tool Approval** in the Command Palette (`workbench.action.chat.editToolApproval`), implemented in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/24b129ba6fcba077a8e7bb42636958a819fbd47f. It lets you inspect and change individual tool approval preferences, including workspace and global approvals, without resetting them all or waiting for a tool invocation. The fix shipped in 1.106.0.

Thanks for the context. The centralized customization editor was implemented in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/405897eb1103a7141acc9113defc0aaa1287a12a through https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/296680. Use **Chat: Open Customizations** (`aiCustomization.openManagementEditor`) or the Customizations button in the Chat header to review and manage customization types in one surface, with descriptions explaining their roles. This completes the original request. The further Agents app navigation and settings-layout improvements are tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/313828. The fix shipped in 1.110.1.

Thanks for the context. https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/af690bd87db3a70924652f5d235121997a442f79 removed the separately styled MCP auto-approval row and passed its approval information into the tool's own presentation part. This addresses the integration and styling mismatch described here. The fix shipped in 1.107.0.

Thanks for the request. This was implemented in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/d68a730e8d9034e7f65ff129fbf29690a0526212: URLs explicitly included in your chat messages are automatically approved, without needing a separate opt-in dropdown choice. For persistent URL or domain approvals, chat.tools.urls.autoApprove provides separate request and response controls rather than granting permission to the entire fetch tool. The fix shipped in 1.107.0.

Thanks for the report. https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/68e1b20ce90dedaf48054b721dbe4b630ff6e143 added horizontal relayout when Quick Chat's toolbar changes size, so switching between models with different label widths now recalculates the input width. This appears addressed by that change. The fix shipped in 1.110.1.

Thanks for the report. This was fixed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/3fe7649e8a92bf62ab62aa6ed97d6684b5c99004: authentication provider selection now checks the full protected-resource URI as well as the authorization server. The two MCP servers therefore use separate resource-specific providers, so Product2's authorization request uses its own resource identifier rather than Product1's. The fix shipped in 1.107.0.

Thanks for the report. This was fixed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/c33015014853aedcb02d69b1b50ef2b80891afce: hiding the selected model now triggers model-selection reconciliation, so the picker switches to the fallback model that will actually handle the request. The fix shipped in 1.122.0.

Thanks for the report. This is resolved by https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/d72d6a24245db6cc9d80988f7cda1305a385037c: policy generation now consumes evaluated configuration data rather than parsing TypeScript source, so `policy.name` can reference a string constant. The current export entry point is `npm run export-policy-data`. The fix shipped in 1.106.0.

Thanks for the report. This leak was fixed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/487cb1e360f3e0108c98396a75bfad62520f60a7: dropdown markdown descriptions are now disposed when replaced and when the dropdown widget is disposed, including descriptions rendered during layout measurement. This addresses the disposable warning reported here. The fix shipped in 1.106.0.

Thanks for the context. This was implemented in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/011ffacbdb366c501e4768ecd15c95150553c790: the MCP server's More... CodeLens menu now offers Sign Out when the account is used only by that server, or Disconnect Account when it is shared with other servers or extensions. This covers the requested entry point while preserving other consumers' access, so this can be closed as completed. The fix shipped in 1.102.0.

Thanks for the report. This was fixed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/5ba9ca4ec1eb57c686052b2f12dee7e236ebb75b: the shared progress indicator now always has a localized accessible name, defaulting to "Progress", including during indeterminate loading. This addresses the missing name shown in your DOM example. The fix shipped in 1.110.1.

Thanks for the request. Thanks for the report. This sign-out/sign-in case was addressed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/d2ff8d16065d4748b8a205bfebdc98d7d76f7864: an already-open issue reporter now refreshes its GitHub token when authentication sessions change, rather than retaining the invalid token. Thanks for the detailed repro and for sticking with this. The flakiness came from the language-feature registry: when your provider and the built-in TypeScript provider scored the same for a file, the tie was broken by registration time, so whichever extension happened to register last won — hence the roughly 50/50 behavior. That tiebreak changed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/edf0b737f34d5050cc04bba08af7a1c509f87678: providers from built-in extensions are now de-prioritized when scores are equal, so a provider from an installed (non-built-in) extension wins consistently. No `extensionDependencies` workaround is needed anymore. Closing as resolved — please open a new issue if you still see a built-in provider taking over on a current build. The fix shipped in 1.78.0.

The User Interface Overview feature, including its static Activity Bar labels and `workbench.action.showInterfaceOverview` command, was removed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/c43e386ec18a4f1a08b342f4f8695f23b5e1c5f2 through https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/175686, so this labeling defect can no longer occur. Thanks for the request. VS Code now uses WebAssembly for its syntax-highlighting engine, implemented in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/a6e59815c82ff654f1754c7858194142d7528f1c. The accompanying https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/95958 includes performance comparisons showing both improvements and workload-specific tradeoffs. Extension business logic can also use WebAssembly behind a JavaScript activation entry point, as explained above. The fix shipped in 1.45.0.
